rule: Fit toward luminance, never toward dE. dE2000 was recorded at every swept value and used to choose nothing; the gap it would have chosen instead is stated below.
instrument: tools/luminance.py -- linear-light Rec.709 relative luminance, mean and p5, over the pose-verified compare spots. Renders captured at the legacy 72 deg camera with each spot's own pitch, 1024 wide.

populationChange.before: 9 spots (2.webp and 10.webp both failed pose verification)
populationChange.now: 10 spots (10.webp flipped true in task 1b; 2.webp is still false)
populationChange.warning: luminance.py filters through delta_e.scorable and has NO --all-spots escape hatch, so this fit is NOT comparable to the committed 0.295, which was fitted on a different population. It is also not comparable to the 2-spot population that produced the figure before plan 4b.

sweep.note: the value shipping before this task

chosen.why: closest mean to the photographs' 0.2924 of any swept value; 0.305 undershoots by 0.0031, 0.31 overshoots by 0.0015

whatTheWrongCriterionWouldHaveChosen.note: dE falls monotonically toward the DARK end of the swept range while luminance says the render is too dark at 0.295. That is the direction-blindness metrics/README.md warns about, visible in one table.

p5Tension.observed: At the chosen 0.31 the render's p5 is 0.0760 against the photographs' 0.0379 -- twice as light. Raising exposure to match the mean makes this worse, not better.
p5Tension.reading: The render's shadows are not as deep as the photographs'. This is the 'reachable blacks' problem plan 3 spent seven tasks on and did not close; exposure cannot fix it, because it is a global multiplier. Recorded here so nobody reads the mean match as a full exposure match.
p5Tension.routed: unowned, same as the wall lightmap atlas

horkyone10Band.criterion: spawn-pooled sRGB luminance (0-255), mean over every spawns[] entry rendered at 480x300 through the full post chain at pixelRatio 1, Rec.709 weights, no linearisation. Same domain as plan 3 task 4's file, NOT comparable to luminance.py's linear scale.
horkyone10Band.harnessDifference: Plan 3 task 4 used Playwright headless Chromium with forced ANGLE/D3D11. This re-derivation ran in the session browser instead, with post.js's chain confirmed live (postOn true on all three). Same method, different host -- treat the absolute numbers as this session's, and the comparison between the three as the result.

reDerived.windowIs: the intersection of the two flats' own +-10 bands, which is how plan 3 task 4 computed [139.0, 148.7] from serenity 138.7 and kings-court 149.0

horkyone10Band.verdict: horkyone-10's shipped 0.42 gives 145.14, inside the re-derived [138.81, 152.18] and 0.36 off its midpoint of 145.50. NOT CHANGED, and checked rather than assumed -- plan 4a task 3 found the then-shipped 0.46 had silently fallen out of its own band, which is why this check is mandatory rather than optional.
